title: Receivables Desk Guidance: Qualifying for the Early-Payment Discount on Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms)
content:
**Rule.** On Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms), where the tier's early-payment discount period is above zero, an invoice paid in full no later than the invoice date plus the tier's early pay discount days earns the tier's early-payment discount percent of its merchandise amount, excluding the components the tier never discounts for early payment, rounded half up to the cent. Calendar days are added to the invoice date, the day after the invoice being day 1, and full payment received on the last day still earns the discount. A partial payment earns nothing, and each invoice earns the discount at most once. Where the tier gives no proportional discount on a partial payment, a partial payment earns no discount.

## The discount period

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Clock starts from | The invoice date shown on the invoice |
| Length | The tier's early-payment discount period, in calendar days; a period of 0 means no discount |
| Counting | The day after the invoice date is day 1 |
| Last qualifying day | The invoice date plus the period; full payment received on that day still earns the discount |
| Comparison | The date full payment is received must be no later than the last qualifying day |
| Records relied on | The invoice's date and number and the payments received against that invoice number, as Northgate's account records show them |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, 10-day period)

| Invoice date | Day 1 | Last qualifying day | Full payment received | Earns the discount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 May | 7 May | 16 May | 16 May | Yes |
| 6 May | 7 May | 16 May | 17 May | No |
| 25 June | 26 June | 5 July | 5 July | Yes |
| 25 June | 26 June | 5 July | 6 July | No |

## The amount

The discount is the tier's percent of the invoice's merchandise amount, the components never discounted for early payment being left out, and the result is rounded half up to the cent.

*Worked example (hypothetical invoice, 1.0 percent tier).* An invoice totals $899.54: merchandise $800.50, sales tax $64.04 and delivery fees $35.00. Sales tax and delivery fees are left out, so the base is $800.50. 1.0 percent of $800.50 is $8.005, which rounds half up to $8.01. Paid in full within the period, the invoice earns a discount of $8.01, which reduces the amount the business owes on its invoice account.

## Points of judgement

- *Partial payment.* A payment of less than the full invoice inside the period earns nothing.
- *Once per invoice.* An invoice that has already earned the discount does not earn it again.
- *Tier with a period of 0.* The period is not above zero, so no invoice on that tier earns the discount.
